interim_updates.note_text: Softlogic Life Insurance PLC (AAIC.N0000; the former Asian Alliance Insurance PLC, rebranded after Softlogic's acquisition, ticker unchanged) grew Company Gross Written Premium 32.2% YoY to Rs.24,756.7mn for H1 2026, with Net Written Premium up 33.6% to Rs.23,149.9mn (i.e. reinsurance cession grew roughly in line with gross premium). By premium type, Group Life premium was the standout, up 63.5% YoY (Rs.4,112.6mn to Rs.6,726.7mn), while Renewal premium (the largest single component at Rs.10,949.1mn) grew 16.3% and First year premium grew 18.4% to Rs.4,441.3mn. Company Profit Before Tax grew a more modest 7.5% to Rs.1,869.4mn and PAT grew 15.0% to Rs.1,403.7mn -- both well below premium growth -- because Net Insurance Benefits and Claims Paid grew faster than premium (Company: Rs.9,101.7mn to Rs.9,570.4mn) and, more materially, because the Change in Insurance Contract Liabilities reserve movement nearly doubled (Company: Rs.3,311.2mn to Rs.6,057.7mn, +82.9%), consistent with a growing in-force book requiring a larger reserve build. Partly offsetting this, the period's net finance result swung from a net COST of Rs.286.7mn in H1 2025 to a net GAIN of Rs.122.0mn in H1 2026 (Company), a swing of Rs.408.6mn, driven by net exchange gains of Rs.408.2mn on the period's foreign-currency exposure (per Note 8) against interest expense of Rs.210.0mn on leases and borrowings; without that FX swing, PBT growth would likely have been negative rather than +7.5%. Group figures (which for the first time include Softlogic Life Insurance Lanka Limited, the former Allianz Life subsidiary acquired 11 July 2025) show Group GWP of Rs.25,962.9mn and Group PAT of Rs.1,461.3mn, both modestly above the standalone Company figures, but the filing provides no prior-year Group comparative to measure Group-basis YoY growth against.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for AAIC -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. YoY comparison above is built entirely on the COMPANY (standalone) basis, not Group: this filing's Group income-statement column has NO 2025 comparative at all (the Group only exists in its current form from 11 July 2025, when Softlogic Life Insurance Lanka Limited was acquired), so a genuine Group-basis YoY comparison is not possible from this document. operating_profit, gross_profit, cost_of_sales, current_assets, current_liabilities, inventory, trade_receivables and trade_payables are all left blank in the financial_statements rows for both bases -- see the script's field-mapping notes for the insurer-specific rationale for each.
interim_updates.takeaway: Premium growth (GWP +32%) looks strong, but it did not flow through to profit at the same rate (PBT +7.5%, PAT +15.0%) because claims and especially the insurance-liability reserve build both grew faster than premium -- and even the modest PBT growth the company did post was flattered by a Rs.408.6mn favourable swing in net finance result (from a Rs.286.7mn cost to a Rs.122.0mn gain, mostly unrealised FX), which is not a repeatable driver of underlying insurance profitability.
operational_highlights: Company Gross Written Premium +32.2% YoY to Rs.24,756.7mn; Net Written Premium +33.6% to Rs.23,149.9mn.
Group Life premium (the fastest-growing category) +63.5% YoY to Rs.6,726.7mn; Renewal premium (largest category) +16.3% to Rs.10,949.1mn; First year premium +18.4% to Rs.4,441.3mn.
Company PBT +7.5% to Rs.1,869.4mn and PAT +15.0% to Rs.1,403.7mn -- both well below premium growth.
Change in Insurance Contract Liabilities (reserve movement) nearly doubled, Company Rs.3,311.2mn to Rs.6,057.7mn (+82.9%), the largest single drag on profit growth.
Net finance result swung from a Rs.286.7mn net cost to a Rs.122.0mn net gain (Company), driven by Rs.408.2mn of net exchange gains -- a Rs.408.6mn favourable swing that flattered PBT growth.
Group total assets Rs.81,595.8mn and Group PAT Rs.1,461.3mn now include Softlogic Life Insurance Lanka Limited (former Allianz Life), acquired 11 July 2025 for a cash consideration of Rs.1,426mn.
key_drivers: Insurance contract liabilities reserve build: Company Rs.3,311.2mn to Rs.6,057.7mn (+82.9%) -- the single largest factor holding back profit growth relative to premium growth.

Net exchange gains of Rs.408.2mn (within Note 8 Finance Cost) swung the net finance line from a Rs.286.7mn cost to a Rs.122.0mn gain -- the main reason PBT still grew despite reserve pressure; this is a market-driven, non-recurring-in-nature item rather than an operating improvement.
Group Life premium segment (+63.5% YoY) is the fastest-growing premium category and a disproportionate share of GWP growth.

Softlogic Life Insurance Lanka Limited acquisition (completed 11 July 2025, Rs.1,426mn consideration) is the first period this subsidiary is consolidated into Group figures, so Group-vs-Company deltas this quarter partly reflect that addition rather than organic growth.
